content.text: {"answers": [{"question_id": "Q1", "question": "What event or action currently starts the summarization process after a meeting ends — for example, does a specific person manually initiate it, or is it triggered automatically by a system such as a calendar or conferencing tool?", "answer": "The minute taker manually initiates it by collecting meeting notes or transcript after the meeting."}, {"question_id": "Q2", "question": "How is the meeting summary currently created — is it written manually by a participant, derived from a recorded transcript, or generated with the help of an automated or AI-based tool?", "answer": "The minute taker drafts it from collected notes or transcript. Automated extraction is an opportunity, not current practice."}, {"question_id": "Q3", "question": "How is the list of email recipients determined — is it always the set of meeting attendees, a predefined distribution list, or does the sender decide case by case?", "answer": "Recipients are \"relevant recipients.\" Exact determination method is not specified."}, {"question_id": "Q4", "question": "Does the summary need to be reviewed or approved by anyone before the email is sent, and if so, who holds that responsibility?", "answer": "Unclear items are confirmed with decision owners before drafting. No formal approval step is specified."}, {"question_id": "Q5", "question": "What content is expected to appear in the summary email — for instance, is it a free-form narrative, or must it include structured elements such as action items, owners, and deadlines?", "answer": "Structured: decisions, action items, and owners are required. Supporting materials may be attached."}, {"question_id": "Q6", "question": "Is there a target or maximum time limit within which the summary email must be sent after the meeting concludes?", "answer": "No time limit is specified."}]}
